chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Chuckles' wedding on stage with Erskine Hawkins
summary: On tour with Erskine Hawkins in Baltimore, Chuckles marries his fiancee on the theatre stage with Green as best man.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: So, now, we're coming to the '40's and I'm particularly interested in your relationship with Chuckles and how that was developing and what really happened to you two during the '40's.

Well, now, we were with the Alabama State Gabriel (unintelligible) wich was Erskine Hawkins -- and still is Erskine Hawkins. And we was in Baltimore, Maryland, the home of the Harlem allstar, Baby Lawrence, and Chuckles' girlfriend was going to visit him -- his fiance, I should say, and he had gotten me to agree to be the best man. Now, the rumor got out

that he was going to become a husband -- at last. So, everybody that was in the show -- they loved Chuckles, see. He was that way, kind of infectious on people. So, he wanted to involve the audience, you know, and they wanted everybody to know that he was going to become a husband, you see. And so now (unintelligible) back stage that got in on him, so they said, "Well, why don't we get a -- we'll ride out front of the theater in taxis and the bus -- you know, a well, charter a bus, and the bride and groom and the best man and the bride, you know, and they're walking in front of the theatre walk (unintelligible) and the band will be playing "Here Comes the Bride," right on through the audience, right on up on the stage to the Reverand (unintelligible) you see." So, that's what we done. And they had a very -- a great jazz sound, Erskine Hawkins. Yeah. What did they call it? Tuxedo -- what was his orchestra called -- Erskind Hawkins? They had a special name -- some kind of special title -- Erskine Hawkins and his Band -- it was something else he was called. Tuxedo Boys -- I think that's what it was. Yes. Because eventually he mentioned it they introduced a jazz sensation that became famous -- "Tuxedo Junction", and most of the bands played it. Well, we got up there on stage and I gave the bride away and she's beautiful, she was. Wow! I couldn't blame my partner, you know. Chuckles had been working 18 years to come to that height in the profession of show business what was known as stardom, you see. Now, imagine how I felt, see. Chuckles -- I was like a brother
